profile.topic: When do simple summaries discard decision-relevant information? (synthetic onboarding exercise)

candidates.source: Edge lists and metadata in the synthetic graph exercise.
candidates.claim: There exist connected graphs with the same degree multiset and different diameters.
candidates.search_trace: Textbook graph invariants already distinguish degree sequence and diameter. This is a known-property teaching exercise, not a novelty claim.
candidates.difference: No novelty for the bare existence claim.
candidates.risk: An exercise may look like a research contribution when scope is omitted.
candidates.first_probe: Compute distances on two labelled graphs.
candidates.advance_if: A connected pair with equal sorted degrees has unequal diameter.
candidates.stop_if: The proposed pair has unequal degree multisets or equal diameter.

candidates.source: Transfer key deduplication to rate-limited synthetic event streams.
candidates.claim: Distinct-key admission under a shared alert cap can reduce missed incidents on a fixed duplicate-heavy stream.
candidates.search_trace: Search budgeted event detection, duplicate alert suppression and incident recall; nearest work not yet verified in this example.
candidates.difference: Compare first-budget versus first-distinct-key at an identical cap on the same stream; novelty unknown.
candidates.risk: Repeated keys can also be independent true incidents.
candidates.advance_if: More distinct incidents found at the same budget on the bounded stream.
candidates.stop_if: Advantage disappears when keys are not a proxy for incident identity.
